==English==

===Etymology===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*ḱel- (cover)}}
{{inh+|en|enm|halle||hall}}, from {{inh|en|ang|heall||hall, dwelling, house, palace, temple, law-court}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*hallu||hall}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*hallō||hall}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*ḱel-||to hide, conceal}}.

Cognate with {{cog|sco|hall, haw||hall}}, {{cog|nl|hal||hall}}, {{cog|de|Halle||hall}}, {{cog|da|hal||hall, sports centre}}, {{cog|fo|høll||hall, palace}}, {{cog|is|höll||palace}}, {{cog|no|hall||hall}}, {{cog|sv|hall||hall}}, {{cog|la|cella||room, cell}}, {{cog|sa|शाला|tr=śā́lā||house, mansion, hall}}. {{dbt|en|cell|cella}}.

* {{IPA|en|/hoːl/|a=SSB,AU,NZ}}
* {{a|en|US}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# A [[corridor]]; a [[hallway]].
#: {{ux|en|The drinking fountain was out in the '''hall'''.}}
#* {{RQ:Lincoln Pratt's Patients|page=304|passage=We tiptoed into the house, up the stairs and along the '''hall''' to the door of the room where the Professor had been spending so much of his time.}}
# A large [[meeting room]].
#: {{ux|en|The hotel had three '''halls''' for conferences, and two were in use by the convention.}}
# A [[manor house]] (originally because a [[magistrate]]'s court was held in the hall of his mansion).
#: {{ux|en|The duke lived in a great '''hall''' overlooking the sea.}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Taming of the Shrew|2|1|passage=But Kate, the prettiest Kate in Christendome, Kate of Kate-'''hall'''.}}
# A building providing student accommodation at a [[university]].
#: {{ux|en|The student government hosted several social events so that students from different '''halls''' would intermingle.}}
# The principal room of a [[secular]] [[medieval]] building.
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} Cleared passageway through a crowd, as for dancing.
#* {{RQ:Jonson Tale of a Tub|passage=Then cry, a '''hall''', a '''hall'''! Come, father Rosin, with your fiddle now.}}
# A place for special [[professional]] [[education]], or for conferring professional [[degree]]s or licences.
#: {{ux|en|a Divinity '''Hall'''; Apothecaries' '''Hall'''}}
# {{lb|en|India}} A [[living room]]. <!--see also BHK-->
# {{lb|en|Oxbridge}} A [[college]]'s [[canteen]], which is often but not always [[coterminous]] with a traditional hall.
# {{lb|en|Oxbridge slang}} A meal served and eaten at a college's hall.
